subject: EU evidence hold: log export checklist & timelines
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acme-cyber.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 12:14:00 +0000
Subject: Request: EU log hold + export details for FinSolve incident

Michael —

Following our call this morning, FinSolve has asked us to preserve and collect server logs and access traces for a suspected data-exposure incident affecting their EU tenant. They requested: a) an explicit written hold timeline for all relevant logs, b) a manifest of artifacts available for export (s3 access logs, inference request traces, KV cache slices, audit events), and c) confirmation that exports stay within EU regions (no US egress).

Can Redwood provide a checklist of what you can export, the typical turnaround time, and the recommended retention window for forensic review? Also please note FinSolve’s compliance team requires chain-of-custody documentation for any artifacts we receive.

We can accept exports to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket in eu-west-1 controlled by our external forensics environment, but if you have constraints (private deployment / VPC-only exports) let us know.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Ross
Lead Incident Analyst, Acme Cyber Ops

--
attachment: request_summary.txt (text)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acme-cyber.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: EU log hold + export details for FinSolve incident

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can place a legal/forensic hold on relevant telemetry and provide an export that remains in eu-west-1; turnaround depends on scope but initial manifest within 8 business hours is typical, full staged export 24-72 hours.

Checklist (high level):
- Artifacts we can produce: inference_request_logs (token-level metadata, no content by default), request_headers, request_timestamps, routing/region tags, per-request model_variant ids, audit_events (auth, config changes), node-level infra logs (scheduler, GPU traces) — note: raw user prompt content requires explicit custodian consent if present in logs.
- Sampling/size options: full slice (all matching requests), time-boxed window (e.g., 48h), or hashed-sample for higher volumes.
- Export formats: compressed CSV/NDJSON for logs; redaction script applied as requested.
- Chain of custody: we’ll attach a prefilled chain_of_custody template and checksum manifest.

Attachments: forensic_log_manifest.csv (stub), redwood_chain_of_custody_template.pdf

Questions for you:
1) Do you require original payloads (full prompt text)? If yes, we need FinSolve authorization and a scoped data transfer agreement.
2) Do you confirm the destination S3 bucket ARN and that it is in eu-west-1 (no cross-region replication)?

Neha / Priyom — looping you in to confirm retention/hold policy and export process below. I’ll coordinate the manifest and assign export owner once we agree scope.

-Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Security & Escalations
Redwood Inference

--
attachment: forensic_log_manifest.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Emily Ross <emily.ross@acme-cyber.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: EU log hold + export details for FinSolve incident

Emily / Michael —

Operational details and constraints:
- Hold start: immediate (we’ll set internal retention flags and disable any automated deletion for matching keys).
- Recommended forensic retention window on our side: 180 days full-fidelity, with a 30/60/90 day staged deletion ramp for derivative indexes unless extended by legal hold. FinSolves compliance asked for 180 days; we can commit to that for this matter, but need explicit ticketed approval (email thread is OK) to keep beyond standard tenant retention.
- Export staging: we can drop artifacts into a pre-authenticated S3 staging area in eu-west-1. For Private deployments where the customer requires VPC-only egress, we’ll coordinate an edge-stage pull into their VPC. If the tenant is on Private, provide the VPC S3 endpoint details.
- Redaction: by default we will redact full-text prompt/response content unless authorized. Redaction is reversible only if we provide an encrypted original archive under a strict chain-of-custody.
- Chain-of-custody: we will provide checksums (sha256), an HSM-signed manifest if requested, and an internal access audit log covering who touched the files. Please fill out the chain_of_custody template with the receiving party details.

Action items assigned: Priyom — prepare export job and estimate size; Michael — coordinate legal approval if full payload is requested; Emily — share S3 ARN and whether FinSolve requires encrypted-in-transit + KMS key in their account or if Redwood will stage with a Redwood-managed key.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
attachment: redwood_chain_of_custody_template.pdf (pdf)

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acme-cyber.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:07:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: EU log hold + export details for FinSolve incident

Neha / Michael —

Thanks, that scope is perfect. FinSolve confirms:
- Destination S3 ARN: arn:aws:s3:::finsolve-forensics-eu-west-1-staging (no replication, bucket policy locked to our Acme forensic role)
- We require encrypted-in-transit and server-side encryption using a customer-managed KMS key in eu-west-1. We will provide the KMS key alias and an IAM role.
- FinSolve compliance also asked that original, unredacted prompt/response payloads be preserved for 180 days but handed to them only after we provide a signed transfer acknowledgment; Acme can act as the custodian.

We can accept the HSM-signed manifest and the SHA256 checksums. Please also include an export ETA — our operations needs to schedule downstream analysis.

Emily
Emily Ross
Lead Incident Analyst, Acme Cyber Ops

--

Emily / team —

Confirming next steps and owners:
- Hold placed: Redwood retention flag enabled at 09/09/2026 13:05Z for all artifacts matching tenant "finsolve-prod".
- Exports: Priyom to run staging export to arn:aws:s3:::finsolve-forensics-eu-west-1-staging (eu-west-1) using customer-provided KMS key. ETA: manifest in 6 hours, full export in ~36 hours.
- Chain-of-custody: Michael to sign the initial transfer acknowledgment once the HSM-signed manifest is available. Emily — please return the filled chain_of_custody template with receiving party fields by EOD tomorrow.
- Retention: Redwood will preserve full-fidelity artifacts for 180 days unless FinSolve requests extension. After the retention window we will securely delete originals and can provide an archived index on request.
- Compliance note: if FinSolve requires data to never leave their VPC (private deployment), we need the exact VPC export endpoint; export flow will change to a pull model and ETA will extend.

Attachments: forensic_log_manifest.csv (manifest preview).

Priyom — please open internal ticket (JIRA-1428) and include export size estimate and access keys rotation plan.

Thanks everyone — I’ll follow up with the signed acknowledgement and the DocuSign link for the transfer once the manifest is finalized.

-Michael
Michael Grant

Redwood Inference
